name: signaling_message.v1
description: Signaling WebSocket envelope (docs/13 §6): control plane only — SDP offer/answer, trickle ICE, teardown, keepalive — on wss://<voice-worker>/v1/signal. Media and context never ride this socket (ADR-4). Every frame wears {v, type, payload}. Forward compatibility (docs/13 §9): new message types are additive within v1, so a receiver MUST ignore frames whose type it does not recognize instead of erroring, and MUST ignore unknown envelope fields — which is why this schema deliberately does not set additionalProperties: false.

v.description: Envelope version. Breaking changes bump this to 2 in lockstep with the /v2 REST path (docs/13 §9).

type.description: The v1 signaling message set (docs/13 §6). Additive within v1: a client MUST ignore frames whose type is unknown (docs/13 §9).

payload.description: Per-type payload — see $defs, dispatched by the oneOf below.

offer_payload.description: client → server. Initial SDP offer — the client is always the offerer; the offer carries the mic track and the ctx data channel in one SDP. Also re-sent (created with iceRestart: true) for ICE restart over the same WebSocket (docs/13 §6, §6.1).

answer_payload.description: server → client. aiortc's answer to the current offer (docs/13 §6).

ice_payload.description: Both directions. One trickled ICE candidate; candidate: null marks end-of-candidates (docs/13 §6).

candidate.description: candidate-attribute string, or null to signal end-of-candidates.

bye_payload.description: Both directions. Clean teardown (docs/13 §6); every hang-up path converges on the same terminal session state (docs/13 §2.2).

error_payload.description: server → client. code uses the docs/13 §1.1 vocabulary — the same code strings as REST. Deliberately NOT an enum here: new codes may be added within an existing prefix class without a version bump, and clients switch on the prefix class when the member is unknown (docs/13 §1.1, §9).

keepalive_payload.description: Both directions, shared by ping and pong. 10 s keepalive; two missed pongs mark the WebSocket dead (docs/13 §6).
